# SPEC — GoAI

Go-native AI library, full spectrum, Pure-Go-first / cgo-last.
Encoding: caveman (see `FORMAT.md`). Target Go 1.26.
Source research: `docs/research/00-landscape.md`. Framing: `PLANNING_PROMPT.md`.

WORKER SUB-SPECS (hardware-capability-scoped, one per secondary machine; this root spec = cross-platform truth, sub-specs record host-specific SIMD/GPU work + measured A/B by capability):
- `SPEC-worker-linux-amd64-cuda.md` — Linux/amd64 (Zen 3 AVX2+FMA CPU-SIMD) + NVIDIA RTX 3060 (CUDA/cuBLAS). Owns §T11b/§T74 amd64-SIMD + the CUDA backend, PR-only. = THE single derived runner spec for that machine (consolidation 2026-07-15): hardware capabilities (§H/§Iw/§CPU/§GPU/§GAP/§PERF), task log (§Tw), runner protocol (§RUN — PR/merge/gates/GPU discipline, worker deltas over LOOP.md), local model assets (§MODELS — formerly models/README.md).

## §G — goals

G1: idiomatic modular Go lib ∀ AI domains — linalg, autograd, classic-ML, deep-learning, NLP/LLM-inference, CV, RL, probabilistic.

G2: core ops → as close as possible to C/C++ refs (Eigen, OpenBLAS, oneDNN, ggml, ONNX Runtime, PyTorch/ATen) via Pure-Go-SIMD; GPU/NPU only where needed.

G3: correctness before speed. ∀ op → valid Pure-Go reference first, optimize as separate step.

G4: math/scientific grounding ! per unit; numeric decisions (stability, accuracy, overflow) documented ≠ implicit.

G5: numeric parity = acceptance. "done" → results match ref within fixed tolerance, proven ≠ claimed.

G6: perf measurable | ⊥ exist. no "faster" without benchmark + baseline compare.

G7: native macOS & Windows & Linux on CPU & GPU & (later) NPU. ∀ accel op → Pure-Go fallback runs everywhere.

"vollwertig" (measurable): L0–L3 green + parity ∀ ops; ≥1 optimized CPU backend beating scalar ref w/ V-BENCH numbers; safetensors IO; ≥1 end-to-end trained model converging; ≥1 GPU backend gated by V-CGO; ≥1 LLM inference path.

## §C — constraints

C1: target Go 1.26. `CGO_ENABLED=0` = default build, ! green ∀ platforms.

C2: cgo-LAST policy = measurable gate. Pure Go default (experimental `simd/archsimd` via `GOEXPERIMENT=simd` on AMD64; Plan9-NEON on ARM64; `avo`; goroutines). cgo/external-C only as optional build-tag backend when ALL hold:
  (1) Pure-Go version §V-green & optimized to ceiling (documented stages + roofline).
  (2) benchmark beats §C.thr vs that optimized Pure-Go version.
  (3) `CGO_ENABLED=0` stays fully functional (fallback everywhere).
  ⊥ all 3 → reject cgo, park idea in §B.
C3 (thr): "deutlich" threshold = speedup ≥ 1.5× OR reaches ≥ 80% of C++ baseline that Pure-Go cannot. revisable → ADR. [B1]

C4: dtypes f32 & f64 first; f16, bf16, int8 later.

C5: tensor layout row-major + strides/views.

C6: GPU → cgo unavoidable (no Pure-Go GPU path). GATING NUANCE (§R47, §T47): Metal needs NO build-tag — macOS system frameworks always present → guarded by `darwin && cgo` only, auto-included on native macOS builds (cgo = default). CUDA/Vulkan stay behind opt-in build-tags because libcublas/-lvulkan are build-time LINK deps not guaranteed present; runtime dlopen (libcuda.so/libvulkan.so.1) is the documented future path to make them tag-free too. All still cgo-gated → `CGO_ENABLED=0` pure-Go build unaffected (§V7).

C7: NPU (ANE/CoreML, DirectML, oneDNN) = explicit non-goal of first stage. re-eval after GPU. ⊥ silent promise.

C8: ⊥ commit | push without explicit user permission. loop works in working-tree only.

C9: deps minimal. Pure-Go path ⊥ pull cgo deps. accel backends isolate deps behind build-tags.

C13: PUBLIC-API DOC GATE. SCOPE (user feedback 2026-07-13): applies to documentation with a HUMAN target audience — godoc, README, docs/*, runnable Examples; texts expected to be read by an LLM only (SPEC.md, FORMAT.md, LOOP.md, PLANNING_PROMPT.md) are EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED from the layperson rule (caveman/dense form stays). ∀ exported symbol in a PUBLIC pkg (non-internal, non-backend-impl) → godoc comment present (DUAL-AUDIENCE per C10 even for SIMPLE methods: professional + layperson); ∀ human-audience feature docs → where applicable BOTH a simple/easy example AND a complex/advanced one (C10's three-level ladder trivial/use-case/embedded already implements this — the gate keeps at least the per-type+per-method floor mechanical, the simple+complex pair stays a review criterion); ∀ exported STRUCT FIELD → own doc/inline comment (fields = public-facing API too; "docs for everything public facing" [user feedback]); ∀ user-facing pkg → ≥1 runnable Example; ∀ exported user-facing TYPE → shown in a runnable Example (its name, New`<Type>` ctor, or ExampleType); ∀ exported METHOD on a user-facing type → shown in a runnable Example too (method name invoked in any Example body, or a dedicated ExampleType_Method) [user feedback 2026-07-13: "a meaningful usage example for every type and every method, plus layperson and professional explanations, where necessary"] — even simple types/methods, "where meaningful" (types/methods where an example is not meaningful — interfaces, functional-option/callback func types, enums, config structs, fixture-heavy models, trivial accessors already exercised by their type's example — go on the justified typeExampleExempt / methodExampleExempt allowlists). ENFORCED mechanically by internal/apicheck (§V19), a test in the suite + `make apicheck`, part of `all`/`ci` → commit/push BLOCKED while red. backend impl subpkgs (ref/cpu/cuda/metal/vulkan/npu) + internal/* EXEMPT (registered via blank import, not user-called surface). turns C10/§V17 from convention into a hard gate. [user feedback]

C18: FURTHER READING MANDATORY [user directive 2026-07-13]. ∀ documentation of implementations, novel algorithms, methods (godoc pkg docs, docs/*.md, README feature sections) → wherever possible reference FURTHER READING the interested reader can use to go deeper: the defining paper (already required by C10/V16) PLUS surveys/books/canonical texts where they exist (e.g. Goodfellow et al. Deep Learning; Sutton & Barto RL; Jurafsky & Martin SLP; the llama.cpp/HF docs for format/ecosystem topics). Depth-entry points are part of the deliverable, ⊥ optional garnish.

C20: ABBREVIATIONS ALWAYS EXPLAINED [user directive 2026-07-14]. ∀ human-audience documentation → every abbreviation/acronym is EXPANDED AND EXPLAINED at first use, preferably in layman terms (e.g. "GQA (grouped-query attention: several query heads share one key/value head, shrinking the cache)"; "GGUF (llama.cpp's single-file model format)"). Applies to godoc, README, docs/*; LLM-only texts (SPEC/FORMAT/LOOP) exempt per C13. Review criterion + sweep (T608); candidate for a soft apicheck heuristic (ALL-CAPS token without a following parenthetical) if the sweep shows it automatable.

C21: RESEARCH-GROUNDED DEFAULTS + KNOB DOCS [user directive 2026-07-14]. ∀ configuration knob (functional options, config struct fields, CLI flags, sampler/optimizer/tokenizer params): (1) DEFAULT VALUE ! grounded in /research wherever possible — the recommended value from literature/industry practice (papers, reference implementations: torch/llama.cpp/HF), so out-of-the-box behavior = best average performance/output, ⊥ fiddling required; (2) doc of every knob = DUAL AUDIENCE (layman + professional, per C10/C13) covering: what the knob does, behavior AT and NEAR its value boundaries (what degrades/saturates as you approach min/max), special values w/ special semantics explicitly documented (e.g. 0 = disabled, -1 = unbounded, nil = auto); (3) ALWAYS cite the research/reasoning behind the chosen default (§R row or external source; further-reading links per C18) — "why THIS default" is part of the doc, ⊥ bare numbers. audit of existing knobs vs C21 → new §T task. [user directive]

C22: NEVER IDLE — HARD RULE [user directive 2026-07-14, EMPHATIC: "auf gar keinen fall ge-idlet werden darf"]. NO holding, NO idling, NO waiting-and-doing-nothing, EVER. The C16 push throttle gates PUSHING ONLY, ⊥ WORKING: committing locally is UNTHROTTLED, only the PUSH waits for the window. While blocked on a push window / CI / a wakeup → ALWAYS do productive work LOCALLY. DEFAULT work = PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATIONS (beat the Python/C++/torch incumbents — §perf-gap, T620 conv rungs, and every measured A/B rung = one §T + docs/benchmarking.md row); else research/tests/docs/audits. If the main context is SATURATED → DELEGATE to worktree-isolated fresh-context SUBAGENTS (proven pattern §T620: vulkan fused conv +20%, measured A/B) — saturation is NEVER a reason to idle, it is a reason to delegate. "nothing safe/unblocked to do" is ⊥ a valid idle excuse: there is ALWAYS a perf rung to attempt+measure or a task to advance. A bare "hold until the push window" wakeup with NO work performed = a C22 VIOLATION. Each LOOP fire while blocked MUST start or advance real work (own or delegated), not merely reschedule. [user directive]

C23: CONFIGURABLE HETEROGENEOUS EXECUTION [user directive 2026-07-14]. backend assignment ! be PER-OP-PART configurable — different backends for different pieces of ONE operation (some layers/rows/tiles on GPU, others on CPU-SIMD) WHERE IT MAKES SENSE. The MECHANISM is REQUIRED (a config surface: per-op / per-layer backend override, composable with C11's zero-config auto-select). DEFAULT = the measured-best single backend; a per-op split on a device that FITS IN VRAM is a transfer≫compute LOSS (ADR-0008/ADR-0021/§C3), so the split is OFF by default and ENABLED only when (a) measured beneficial, or (b) forced by C24 (low-VRAM). ⊥ silently split — the routing is explicit + documented (C21 knob docs). [user directive]

C24: LOW-END / LOW-VRAM FUNCTIONAL [user directive 2026-07-14]. GoAI ! run on low-end devices with LITTLE-TO-NO VRAM — SLOWER there, but FUNCTIONAL, NEVER a hard failure. NO hard VRAM floor. When a model exceeds device VRAM → transparently offload the overflow to CPU-SIMD (llama.cpp-style partial/layer offload — THIS is the legitimate use of C23's split: FUNCTIONALITY, not speed). CGO_ENABLED=0 pure-Go path stays fully functional everywhere (§V7/§C1). Graceful degradation, ⊥ crash / ⊥ OOM-abort when a fallback exists. [user directive]

C25: GLOBAL-SCALE PERF MANDATE [user directive 2026-07-14, EMPHATIC: "IMMER bis auf das letzte prozent optimieren"]. GoAI is an AI library → at popularity it runs on MILLIONS-to-BILLIONS of devices, so EVERY 1% perf gain = a huge GLOBAL compute + energy saving. ALWAYS optimize to the LAST PERCENT on hot paths: DEVIRTUALIZE + INLINE maximally (dtype-switch-ONCE typed `[]T` kernels — ⊥ per-element interface dispatch / closure / Unravel-alloc, §base-perf-sweep), hoist invariants out of loops, zero allocation on the per-element/per-token path, measure every rung (§V22 A/B). "good enough" is ⊥ acceptable on a hot path; the roofline ceiling is the target. This is the WHY behind C22 (never idle → the idle default is perf): the global compute footprint. [user directive]

C26: RECURSIVE DECOMPOSE → BOTTOM-UP VERIFIED ASSEMBLY [user directive 2026-07-15]. ∀ complex/hard task → recursively DECONSTRUCT into smaller subtasks, subtasks into sub-subtasks, until each LEAF is small enough to implement AND verify for correctness IN ISOLATION (unit test ∨ parity ∨ gradcheck ∨ collapse-test pins it @ tight tol). THEN assemble BOTTOM-UP: build each higher level ON the already-verified leaves. RATIONALE: a leaf verified in isolation eliminates bugs AT THAT LEVEL, ∴ a defect surfacing at a higher level is LOCALIZED to the NEW composition (verified leaves ruled out) → cheap fault-localization, only the higher-level integration test needs re-checking; a top-only-checkable big-bang hides an unbounded bug-search. Established stepwise-refinement ∨ divide-and-conquer ∨ modular-decomposition + test-pyramid discipline (§R247, §R248, §R249). ALREADY the repo's feature pattern: collapse-test pins base-equivalence @1e-10 → per-param gradcheck → e2e only checks integration (T654/T655/T660); the worktree-subagent split (C22) is decomposition at the task level. Composes with G3 (reference-first), G5 (parity=acceptance, proven≠claimed), C22 (decomposition ALWAYS yields a small next task → never idle), C25 (leaf-level verification protects hot-path micro-opts). ⊥ ship a composite whose correctness can only be asserted at the top. [user directive]

C19: INTERNAL UTILITIES = GO [user directive 2026-07-14]. ∀ internal tooling that does NOT require the AI-Python stack (numpy/torch golden generation stays .venv) → implement in GO, ⊥ python. Includes simple jobs like table rendering. Existing python utilities in that class get ported when touched; .venv remains ONLY for reference-library parity (goldens, torch comparisons).

C17: CI WARNINGS = ERRORS [user directive 2026-07-13]. ∀ warning in a CI run (runner deprecations, action deprecations, tool warnings in logs) = a defect requiring a fix task — ⊥ ignore, ⊥ suppress without root-cause fix. Known open instance: Node-20 deprecation from actions/checkout@v4 + actions/setup-go@v5 (→T586). CI watches must REPORT warnings, not only conclusions.

C16: PUSH THROTTLE [user directive 2026-07-13; amended 2026-07-14]. push to github MAX once per HOUR — batch completed tasks into local commits, push the batch when ≥1h since last push. EXCEPTION 1: changes to the CI-CLI optimizer itself (internal/cichange, .github/workflows/*) push IMMEDIATELY (they need live CI verification). EXCEPTION 2 [2026-07-14]: pushes that consume ZERO CI minutes may go out anytime — i.e. the diff matches the workflow-level paths-ignore filesystem patterns (root *.md + docs/**, →T609) so NOT A SINGLE runner starts. EXCEPTION 3 [2026-07-16, user directive "throttle bypass spec only changes that need to be passed to the main agent"]: a SPEC-ONLY change that passes a task/finding to the MAIN AGENT (a §T row surfacing a cross-machine lever — e.g. T762 MoE sparse-decode) push+merge IMMEDIATELY, ⊥ wait the hour — it is main-agent COORDINATION + doc-only (root SPEC.md ∈ *.md = zero-runner, subsumed by EXC2), so throttling only DELAYS the main agent picking it up. ALL other pushes (perf/code PRs) stay ≤1/hr per the base rule. loop bookkeeping: record last-push time; a CI watch per push stays mandatory for runs that do start.

C15: NO MAGIC STRINGS. identifier-like string literals (backend names, …) = TYPED constants/enums, ⊥ bare literals. backend.Name string-enum (backend.CPU/Ref/Metal/CUDA/Vulkan); Get/SetPreference/Register/Name() all typed. exception: a string literal that IS an enum's canonical value definition (backend/names.go) or an existing typed enum's Stringer (tensor.DeviceKind → tensor/device.go). enforced mechanically (§V21). [ADR-0015, §C12, user feedback]

C14: TYPED OP PARAMS. op-parameter surface = idiomatic typed Go, ⊥ `map[string]any`. `backend.Attrs` = sealed interface, one typed struct per op w/ dual-audience field docs (§C13) + a `WithDefaults()` shared by kernel & VJP (defaults ⊥ drift). construction = compile-checked struct literal; a wrong field/type = compile error, ⊥ silent default. specialization of §C12 for the dispatch layer. [ADR-0014, §I6, §V20, user feedback]

C12: IDIOMATIC Go. ∀ public API → idiomatic Go conventions. In particular FUNCTIONAL OPTIONS (variadic `...Option`) for functions with ≥2 optional/config params instead of long positional lists (Rob Pike self-referential-fn pattern; required tensors stay positional, hyperparams become options w/ defaults, guard invalid). e.g. nn.DPO/IPO/KTO(ctx, …tensors, opts ...PrefOption) w/ nn.Beta/ReferencePoint/DesirableWeight/UndesirableWeight. single well-named param MAY stay positional (⊥ over-abstract). [user feedback]

C11: ZERO-CONFIG accel = default UX. user does as little as possible to run on GPU/accel: cgo/build-tags are the ONLY gating (which backends compile in); at runtime each compiled-in backend self-detects (device present → Register in init) & the highest-preference registered one is auto-selected (§V18). user ⊥ required to write backend-selection code; MAY override order via backend.SetPreference or pick per-call via Context.WithBackend. no C toolchain / C libs → those cgo backends simply absent, pure-Go path still runs (§V7). NPU stays non-goal (§R45).

C10: docs = first-class deliverable, ⊥ afterthought. ∀ public API → godoc for TWO audiences: AI professional (math/algorithm/paper-cite/§R) AND layperson (plain-language what/why/when). PLUS runnable godoc `Example`/`ExampleT_method` fns at MULTIPLE levels: (a) trivial (one call, minimal), (b) ≥1 realistic trivial use-cases, (c) ≥1 complex/EMBEDDED example showing the piece inside a bigger pipeline (e.g. LoRA inside a full fine-tune loop). examples ! compile & pass via `// Output:` (go test). guarded by V17.

## §I — architecture invariants

layer model (strict, top ⊥ know backend internals):

I.L0 core: `Tensor` (data, dtype, shape, strides, device), `Dtype`, `Device`, `Allocator`, views (reshape/slice/transpose = stride ops). ⊥ cgo in L0.

I.L1 compute: `Backend` + `Kernel` interface + Pure-Go reference backend = TRUTH. registry + feature-detection.

I.L1b accel: swappable backends (cpu-simd, cuda, metal, vulkan) behind same interface, feature-detect + fallback.

I.L2 autograd: tape/graph + `Variable` + VJP rules per op.

I.L3 nn: layers, init, optimizer, loss, data pipeline.

I.L4 domains: transformer/LLM, CV, classic-ML, RL, probabilistic.

I.L5 io: safetensors, GGUF, ONNX.

INVARIANTS:

I1: higher layer ⊥ import backend internals. public API backend-agnostic.

I2: ∀ op → Pure-Go fallback exists.

I3: ⊥ cgo in L0.

I4: accel backend selected via feature-detection @ runtime, ⊥ compile-time-only lock; missing accel → fallback.

I5: `CGO_ENABLED=0` build green ∀ {macOS, Windows, Linux}.

I6: op parameters = TYPED. `backend.Attrs` is a SEALED interface (`interface{ opAttrs() }`), one struct per op (AttnAttrs, NormAttrs, RoPEAttrs, …); ⊥ `map[string]any`/stringly-typed keys. construct = checked struct literal; read = comma-ok assert + `WithDefaults()` (defaults single-sourced, kernel+VJP share). Execute/Kernel/Record/VJP signatures unchanged (param stays `Attrs`). [ADR-0014, §C14, §V20]

| R249 | BOTTOM-UP ASSEMBLY + TEST PYRAMID + FAULT-LOCALIZATION (grounds §C26 assemble half): bottom-up integration builds & tests low-level units FIRST, then composes upward, so each new level rests on already-verified parts. The Test Pyramid = many fast, isolated UNIT tests at the base, progressively fewer integration/e2e tests above (base tests are cheap+precise, top tests broad+slow). Verified components SHRINK the defect search space: a failure at a composed level implicates the NEW composition, not the leaves already proven → cheaper fault-localization, only higher-level tests re-checked. Matches the repo pattern: collapse-test pins a base equivalence @1e-10, per-param gradcheck, e2e only checks integration (T654/T655/T660). | Cohn 2009 "Succeeding with Agile" (test pyramid) + Fowler martinfowler.com/bliki/TestPyramid + Beck 2002 "Test-Driven Development" (unit-first) + Myers "The Art of Software Testing" (bottom-up integration) | high |
| R250 | J-LENS / J-SPACE (Anthropic 2026-07-06 "Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models"; ref-impl github.com/anthropics/jacobian-lens Apache-2.0, jlens-paket). FIT: J_l = E[dh_L/dh_l] pro layer — erwarteter input-output-Jacobian final-residual vs layer-l-residual; cotangents ueber target-positionen t2>=t SUMMIERT, dann ueber source-positionen GEMITTELT; korpus ~100-1000 generische web-text-sequenzen a 128 tokens (quality saturiert schnell); merge() = mittelung disjunkter daten-slices (parallelisierbar). READOUT: JL(h_l) = W_U norm(J_l h_l) — logit-lens mit Jacobian-transport in die final-basis, modell-eigenes unembedding, ranked vocab. J-SPACE: aktivierungen darstellbar als SPARSE NONNEGATIVE kombination von <=k J-lens-richtungen (k<=25); occupancy empirisch: richtungen greedy addieren bis rekonstruktions-gewinn unter random-direction-KONTROLLE faellt. ARTEFAKT: .pt-serialisierung (J_l-matrizen + unembed-ref + modell-meta), from_pretrained laedt. VIZ: layer x position slice-grid (HTML, d3): zelle = lens-top-1-wort + vocab-rank-superscript, click-pin -> rank-tracking-charts + rank-heatmap, unterste zeile = echter modell-output. KERN-BEFUND: global-workspace-verhalten — "denk an X, schreib Y" -> J-space zeigt X obwohl output Y ist. T812-KORREKTUR (vs ref-impl gemessen): estimator MASKIERT invalid-positionen — letzte position (kein next-token-target) IMMER + skip_first fuehrende attention-sink-positionen aus target-summe UND source-divisor (n_valid, nicht seq; ref-default skip_first=16 fuer 128er-webtext); .pt-artefakt = torch.save({"J": {int-layer: fp16 [d,d]}, n_prompts, source_layers, d_model}), layer-index = BLOCK-OUTPUT (GoAI l+1), keine identity gespeichert, row-major J[out,in] verbatim. T813-BEFUND: ref-repo enthaelt KEINEN dekompositions-code (erschoepfend gegrept) — J-space-dekomposition ist paper-rezept-only → tier-2 property-anchor (planted-recovery 1e-12, noise-occupancy 0.20, monotone rekonstruktion auf golden-lens). | Anthropic 2026 j-space paper + github.com/anthropics/jacobian-lens (REF-IMPL = tier1 anchor moeglich §V16) | high |
| R251 | LLaDA-style masked discrete diffusion (Nie et al. 2025, arXiv:2502.09992 Eq.3): forward corruption independently replaces each token with one absorbing `[MASK]` state at level t; a bidirectional transformer predicts original tokens; per-sequence objective `1/(L·t)·Σ_masked CE`. Reverse generation starts all-mask and iteratively keeps high-confidence predictions while re-masking the rest. GoAI maps this to Vocab+1, non-causal GPT blocks, differentiable masked-row gather, and a fixed confidence schedule. Validation: hand objective, mask statistics, sampler schedule, full parameter gradcheck and trained grammar e2e. | Nie et al. 2025 arXiv:2502.09992 Eq.3 | high |
| R252 | Cross-Layer Attention / CLA (Brandon et al. 2024, arXiv:2405.12981): adjacent transformer layers form groups; the leader computes K,V once and followers reuse them while retaining their own Q/output/FFN parameters. Thus KV-cache slots fall from Layers to Layers/Share; Share=1 reduces to ordinary per-layer attention. GoAI uses decoupled OpMHA(q,k,v), omits follower Wk/Wv, and stores one decode cache slot per group. Validation: exact Share=1 GPT collapse, fan-out gradient into leader K/V, cache cardinality, Forward/Decode parity and trained e2e. | Brandon et al. 2024 arXiv:2405.12981 | high |
| R253 | Coconut continuous latent reasoning (Hao et al. 2024, arXiv:2412.06769 §3): one continuous thought is the last hidden state fed back directly as the next input embedding; K thoughts create K additional sequential backbone passes and remain differentiable through BPTT. Curriculum stage k replaces the first k textual reasoning steps with k latent thoughts and supervises only the remaining chain/answer tokens; optional begin/end markers delimit latent mode. GoAI validation isolates the mechanism with H-hop pointer chasing: K=0 exact GPT collapse, full feedback gradcheck, and a pause-token equal-position control proving the gain comes from recurrent state rather than added positions. | Hao et al. 2024 arXiv:2412.06769 §3 | high |
| R254 | BitNet b1.58 QAT (Ma et al. 2024 arXiv:2402.17764; Wang et al. 2023 arXiv:2310.11453): a full-precision master weight is fake-quantized each forward by absmean scale gamma=mean(abs(W)) to effective gamma*clamp(round(W/gamma),-1,1), while each activation row uses absmax int8 quantization; STE passes gradients to the masters. RMSNorm precedes activation quantization. Validation pins the three-value grid/gamma, STE gradients, full-precision collapse, convergence and log2(3) bits/weight. | Ma et al. 2024 arXiv:2402.17764 + Wang et al. 2023 arXiv:2310.11453 | high |
| R255 | Process reward models (Lightman et al. 2023 arXiv:2305.20050; Math-Shepherd arXiv:2312.08935; ProcessBench arXiv:2412.06559): score every reasoning step at its end position with a sigmoid scalar head and BCE against hard/soft correctness labels; solution score is the minimum step score, so the weakest step controls best-of-N. Unlike an outcome reward model, step supervision localizes erroneous reasoning and exposes lucky-correct contamination. Validation uses earliest-error F1 and PRM-vs-ORM/random best-of-8 plus full parameter gradcheck. | Lightman et al. 2023 §2/§4.2 + Math-Shepherd Eq.4-5 + ProcessBench | high |
| R256 | EAGLE feature-level speculative decoding (Li et al. 2024 arXiv:2401.15077 §4.1): a small autoregressive head predicts the next base-model feature from current feature plus next-token embedding; the frozen LM head maps drafted features to tokens and a base pass verifies the longest matching prefix, preserving the base distribution/greedy sequence. Training loss is SmoothL1(predicted feature,next feature)+0.1*CE(predicted-feature logits,next token), not MSE. GoAI ships a linear draft chain (candidate tree is follow-up); validation pins the exact loss including abs(d)>1, full gradients and lossless generation for arbitrary heads. | Li et al. 2024 arXiv:2401.15077 §4.1 | high |
| R257 | Byte Latent Transformer / BLT (Pagnoni et al. 2024 arXiv:2412.09871): a separately trained byte LM creates frozen boundaries from next-byte entropy; local byte encoder pools each span into one patch, a causal latent transformer runs over the variable per-forward patch count, and a local decoder cross-attends patches back to byte positions. Dynamic patch count needs no ragged tensor for GoAI's single-sequence rank-2 path. Validation: entropy/patched-length references, span-mask isolation, stride-1 collapse to byte GPT, all-main-parameter gradcheck and trained byte-LM generation. | Pagnoni et al. 2024 arXiv:2412.09871 §2.3/§3 | high |
| R258 | APOLLO (Zhu et al. 2024): project raw full-rank gradient G through a periodically redrawn Gaussian rank-r P, maintain Adam moments on R=PG, derive each output-channel scale as norm(Adam(R) column)/norm(R column), and apply that scale to raw G; norm-growth limiter caps consecutive update-norm growth at gamma=1.01. APOLLO-Mini uses rank 1, one tensor scale, alpha=sqrt(128). Unlike GaLore/Fira it stores no projection matrix: only its random seed, regenerating P when used. | Zhu et al. 2024 arXiv:2412.05270 Eq.4-5 + Algorithm 1 + §4.2 | high |
| R259 | Q-GaLore has four simultaneous storage/scheduling mechanisms, not merely 8-bit Adam state: block-wise INT8 optimizer states; SVD projection stored block-wise INT4; layer-local lazy refresh whose 5-similarity mean at least 0.4 doubles its cadence; model weights persist as block-wise INT8 and are re-quantized after updates with unbiased stochastic rounding. Official defaults include block 256 and gap 200. (A) WSD (Hu/Tu/Han et al. 2024 "MiniCPM" arXiv:2404.06395 §4.2 Eq.1) — modern cosine-alternative for LLM pretrain. THREE phases over step s, peak η, warmup W, decay-start S, half-life H: WSD(s)=(s/W)·η for s<W [LINEAR warmup, s/W NOT (s+1)/W → reaches η at s=W]; =η for W≤s<S [STABLE constant plateau]; =η·0.5^((s−S)/H) for s≥S [EXPONENTIAL decay, halves every H steps]. DEFAULT decay = exponential (paper ablation beats linear/cosine), MiniCPM half-life≈5000 steps≈20B tok, peak η=0.01. Decay DURATION≈10% of total ("10% Steps are Enough", 2.5% falls short) = a training-config choice, NOT a param of f. NO explicit η_min floor (exponential → ≈0; clamp externally if wanted). KEY vs cosine: long constant stable phase → no preset total T, CONTINUE/BRANCH from any stable checkpoint, only final ≈10% decayed. Boundaries continuous (s=W: warmup=stable=η; s=S: stable=decay=η). CORRECTION vs initial assumption: warmup is s/W not (s+1)/W (differs from nn.WarmupCosine's (s+1)/W convention — documented). (B) InverseSqrt/Noam (Vaswani et al. 2017 "Attention Is All You Need" §5.3) — lr=scale·dModel^(−1/2)·min(sₙ^(−1/2), sₙ·W^(−3/2)), sₙ=step+1 (1-indexed); linear rise then 1/√step decay, PEAK at sₙ=W value scale·(dModel·W)^(−1/2), never reaches 0 (slow tail). matches nn.WSD + nn.InverseSqrt (stateless fns, sibling to nn.WarmupCosine). §V16 tier-1: nn/schedule_test.go — WSD exact @1e-12 at all phase boundaries+interior + flat-plateau + continuity; InverseSqrt vs independent formula @1e-12 + closed-form peak + monotonicity + scale-linearity; Example{WSD,InverseSqrt} | Hu et al. 2024 arXiv:2404.06395 §4.2 Eq.1 + Vaswani 2017 §5.3 (PAPER = tier2 final §V16) | high |

| R109 | Gradient checkpointing / activation rematerialization (Chen, Xu, Zhang, Guestrin 2016 "Training Deep Nets with Sublinear Memory Cost" arXiv:1604.06174; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs paper §4.1/§4.3/§5.1 + torch.utils.checkpoint, NOT /deep-research). MECHANISM: a checkpointed segment does NOT store its intermediate activations on the FORWARD (keeps only inputs+final outputs); on BACKWARD its forward is RE-RUN from the saved inputs to regenerate the activations, which feed the local VJPs, then are freed. CORRECTNESS: computes MATHEMATICALLY IDENTICAL gradients to standard backprop — trades one extra forward per segment for memory, NO approximation; recomputation must be DETERMINISTIC (same inputs→same activations) → with deterministic ops the grads are BIT-FOR-BIT identical. | R178 | Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing (Wang, Gao, Chen, Xie & Dai 2024, "Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing Strategy for Mixture-of-Experts", arXiv:2408.15664; the MoE routing of DeepSeek-V3 arXiv:2412.19437 §2.1.2); research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs primary Eq.3 + Algorithm 1 + DeepSeek-V3, NOT /deep-research. | R179 | DropPath / Stochastic Depth (Huang, Sun, Liu, Sedra & Weinberger 2016, "Deep Networks with Stochastic Depth", ECCV, arXiv:1603.09382; modern per-sample form in timm/layers/drop.py, used by DeiT/Swin/ConvNeXt/ViT); research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs primary §3 Eq.2/4/5 + timm drop_path(), NOT /deep-research. | R182 | No-repeat n-gram blocking (HuggingFace NoRepeatNGramLogitsProcessor/_calc_banned_ngram_tokens + fairseq; tri-gram blocking from Paulus, Xiong & Socher 2017 "A Deep Reinforced Model for Abstractive Summarization", arXiv:1705.04304 §2.5); research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs HF source + fairseq sequence_generator.py + Paulus §2.5, NOT /deep-research. | R185 | Flow Matching / Rectified Flow generative objective (Lipman, Chen, Ben-Hamu, Nickel & Le 2022 "Flow Matching for Generative Modeling", arXiv:2210.02747 OT-CFM; Liu, Gong & Liu 2022 "Rectified Flow", arXiv:2209.03003; the objective of Stable Diffusion 3, Esser et al. 2024 arXiv:2403.03206); research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs primary Eq.1-2/9/22-23 + TorchCFM + facebookresearch/flow_matching, NOT /deep-research. (3) Converges in ≤ m steps (m=gen tokens) via FRONT-TO-BACK locking (position 0's prediction never depends on any y ⇒ correct after step 1; position i locks once y_<i fixed); k≪m in practice = the speedup. (1) PRECOND (Table 1): D(x;σ)=c_skip·x+c_out·F(c_in·x; c_noise), c_skip=σ_data²/(σ²+σ_data²), c_out=σ·σ_data/√(σ²+σ_data²), c_in=1/√(σ²+σ_data²), c_noise=ln(σ)/4; σ_data default 0.5. (2) LOSS WEIGHT λ(σ)=1/c_out²=(σ²+σ_data²)/(σ·σ_data)² ⇒ λ·c_out²=1 (uniform effective loss). (3) TRAINING NOISE ln(σ)≈N(P_mean=−1.2, P_std=1.2) [not implemented — one-line caller helper, parked]. (2) consolidation (Eq.5): Ω_k += Σ_{ν} ω_k^ν/((Δθ_k^ν)²+ξ), Δθ_k^ν=total displacement over task ν, ξ damps tiny displacement. | R219 | LLM watermarking — red-green soft watermark + z-score detector (Kirchenbauer, Geiping, Wen, Katz, Miers & Goldstein 2023, "A Watermark for Large Language Models", ICML, arXiv:2301.10226); research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs Algorithm 2 (soft gen) + Eq.3 §4 (z-score) + official github.com/jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking, NOT /deep-research. Averaging the WEIGHTS of several models fine-tuned from the SAME pretrained init (different hp/seed/aug) beats the single best model at NO extra inference cost (soup = one model). DISTINCT from SWA/EMA (§weightavg — snapshot averaging along ONE run) and TIES/DARE/SLERP (interference-aware/geometric merges): a plain mean over INDEPENDENT fine-tunes + a greedy selection. (1) UNIFORM soup = unweighted elementwise mean θ=(1/\|S\|)Σθ_i of ALL models. (2) GREEDY soup (Recipe 1): sort models DECREASING by held-out val accuracy; ingredients←{}; for each in order add iff ValAcc(avg(ingredients∪{θ})) ≥ ValAcc(avg(ingredients)); return avg(ingredients). (3) first (best) model always added (empty init). (4) acceptance ≥ non-decreasing; soup recomputed as uniform mean of current ingredients each add. (5) KEY GUARANTEE: greedy soup never underperforms the best individual model on held-out data (by construction). NUANCE: paper text uses ≥; official repo uses strict > on a running-best — here ≥ (matches paper). eval is a caller callback (accuracy of an averaged weight set). A PEFT INITIALIZATION distinct from LoRA §R27 (random A + zero B ⇒ adapts the weight RESIDUAL) / DoRA §R70 / VeRA §R215: PiSSA SVD-factorizes W and seeds the LoRA matrices from the TOP-r PRINCIPAL components, so training updates the high-singular-value directions (which carry most of the weight) → faster convergence, better optimum. (Eq.2/3) W=U·diag(σ)·Vᵀ; A=U[:,:r]·diag(σ[:r])^½, B=diag(σ[:r])^½·V[:,:r]ᵀ ⇒ A·B = U_r·diag(σ_r)·Vᵀ_r (rank-r principal reconstruction; √σ split EVENLY between A,B). (Eq.4) frozen residual W_res=W−A·B=U[:,r:]·diag(σ[r:])·V[:,r:]ᵀ. (Eq.5) forward Y=X(W_res+A·B)=XW at init ⇒ identity-like start; only A,B train; NO α/r scaling (scale 1), UNLIKE LoRA. Liu & Jialu Liu 2024, "Statistical Rejection Sampling Improves Preference Optimization", ICLR, arXiv:2309.06657); research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs §3.2 + Algorithm 2, NOT /deep-research. A preference-DATA-GENERATION procedure distinct from all preference LOSSES here (DPO/IPO/KTO/CPO/SimPO/ORPO/SLiC/Bradley-Terry/Plackett-Luce): DPO/SLiC fit a model defined w.r.t. the OPTIMAL policy π*(y\|x) ∝ π_sft(y\|x)·exp(r(x,y)/β) but train on pairs from an arbitrary policy — RSO closes the gap by REJECTION SAMPLING from π* (proposal π_sft, RM-scored candidates), keeping a subset distributed as π* to label into pairs for DPO(sigmoid)/SLiC(hinge). NUANCE (research, all 3 agents): Alg.2 recomputes r_max over the NOT-YET-ACCEPTED subset (y∉D_x) iteratively; THIS impl uses the STATIC batch max (the §3.2 acceptance-probability form + a valid rejection sampler, M=exp(r_max/β) bounds the batch) — iterative-M variant parked, documented honestly. VJPs route the gradient to the SELECTED branch (shared "selectVJP" pattern): Maximum da=g where a≥b else 0, db=g where a<b (ties→a, a subgradient choice, measure-zero); Minimum da=g where a≤b; Where da=g where cond≠0, db=g where cond==0, dcond=NIL (non-differentiable mask). Heavily used: max(x,eps) numerical stability, where(mask,·,·) causal/padding masks. matches OpMaximum/OpMinimum/OpWhere + ops.{Maximum,Minimum,Where}. §V16 tier-1/§V2: ops/select_test.go MaximumMinimumWhereForward (max[1,5,3]/[4,2,3]=[4,5,3], min, where[1,0,1]=[a,b,a] select, shape-mismatch errors) + ExampleWhere; autograd/select_test.go Maximum/Minimum/WhereGradcheck (finite-diff, no ties) + MaximumRouting (dg to larger, explicit da/db) | numpy maximum/minimum/where docs + calculus (REF = definitional, no research) | high |
| R130 | Sqrt + Abs + Clip (numpy.sqrt/abs/clip) — DEFINITIONAL math ops, no paper (elementwise, §V16 exempt from research-lite; source = numpy docs + standard calculus for the VJPs). Extends the elementwise family (Exp/Log/Tanh/ReLU/GELU/Sigmoid/SiLU → +Sqrt/Abs/Clip). SQRT: y=√x, VJP dx=g/(2√x)=g/(2y) (undefined at x=0). ABS: y=\|x\|, VJP dx=g·sign(x) (0 at x=0, matching numpy/torch). CLIP(x,Lo,Hi): y=clamp(x,[Lo,Hi]) (Lo≤Hi), VJP dx=g where Lo≤x≤Hi else 0 (gradient passes through the unclipped region — the pattern used for gradient clipping / bounded activations). Sqrt/Abs use the shared unaryKernel/unaryVJP; Clip carries ClipAttrs{Lo,Hi}. Reference kernels (the existing elementwise ops are ref-level; GPU has its own where compute-bound). matches OpSqrt/OpAbs/OpClip + ClipAttrs + ops.{Sqrt,Abs,Clip}. §V16 tier-1/§V2: ops/mathops_test.go SqrtAbsClipForward (√[1,4,9]=[1,2,3], \|·\|, clamp[0,1], Lo>Hi errors) + ExampleClip; autograd/mathops_test.go Sqrt/Abs/ClipGradcheck (finite-diff == derivative) + ClipZeroGradWhenClamped (clamped ends → 0) | numpy sqrt/abs/clip docs + calculus (REF = definitional, no research) | high |
| R129 | Reshape + ExpandDims + Squeeze + Stack (numpy.reshape/expand_dims/squeeze/stack) — DEFINITIONAL, no paper/algorithm (metadata/data-movement ops, §V16 exempt from research-lite; definitional source = numpy docs, per §V16 "kein Paper" clause). RESHAPE: change shape keeping row-major order + element count (out[flat i]=x[flat i]); target Numel must match. Differentiable: VJP reshapes g back to input shape (dx[flat i]=g[flat i]) — a pure re-layout. EXPANDDIMS(x,axis): insert a size-1 axis (rank+1; axis∈[0,ndim], neg from end+1) = Reshape. SQUEEZE(x,axis): remove a size-1 axis (rank−1; errors if that axis≠size 1) = Reshape. STACK(axis,…t): join along a NEW axis (all inputs same shape → rank+1) = ExpandDims each + Concat (§R126); numpy.stack. All differentiable (compose OpReshape + OpConcat, both have VJPs). Memory-bound → ref/cpu, GPU falls back (§I4/ADR-0008). matches OpReshape + ReshapeAttrs{Shape} + ops.{Reshape,ExpandDims,Squeeze,Stack}. §V16 tier-1 (definitional + §V2 gradcheck): ops/reshape_test.go — ReshapeForward (flat order preserved, incompatible-count errors) + ExpandSqueezeRoundTrip (insert/remove size-1, values preserved, squeeze-non-1 errors) + Stack (numpy stack axis0/axis1, result[i]==input i) + Example{ExpandDims,Stack}; autograd/reshape_test.go ReshapeGradcheck (grad reshapes back to preserved flat position) | numpy reshape/stack docs (REF = definitional, no research) | high |
| R128 | Slice + Split (numpy x[start:end] / numpy.split) — DEFINITIONAL, no paper/algorithm (data-movement ops, §V16 exempt from research-lite; definitional source = numpy docs, per §V16 "kein Paper" clause). SLICE: extract the half-open [start,end) along an axis; output = input shape with that axis extent → end−start; each out element copies from x with the axis coord shifted +start; negative axis from end. Differentiable: VJP SCATTERS g back into a zero input-shaped tensor at the sliced range (0 elsewhere). SPLIT: cut x into consecutive sized pieces along an axis (numpy sized split — e.g. a fused QKV projection → Q,K,V); sizes must be positive and sum to the axis extent; built as N Slices → the DUAL of Concat (§R126). Because x feeds N slice ops, the autograd tape ACCUMULATES their scattered grads into the full input gradient (dx = concat of the pieces' grads) — so Split trains through. Memory-bound → ref/cpu, GPU falls back (§I4/ADR-0008). matches OpSlice + SliceAttrs{Axis,Start,End} + backend.SlicePlan (shared fwd/VJP) + ops.Slice(x,axis,start,end) + ops.Split(x,axis,…sizes). §V16 tier-1 (definitional + §V2 gradcheck): ops/slice_test.go — SliceForward (numpy rows/cols + neg axis) + SplitConcatInverse (concat(split)==x, round-trip, uneven sizes) + Errors + Example{Slice,Split}; autograd/slice_test.go — SliceGradcheck (scatter, zero grad outside range) + SplitGradientAccumulation (dx=[wa;wb] stacked = tape sums slice grads) | numpy slice/split docs (REF = definitional, no research) | high |

The SIMPLEST PEFT: prepend a learned soft prompt P∈[k,d_model] (k continuous virtual-token embeddings) to the input token embeddings X∈[seq,d_model] → model input [P;X]∈[k+seq,d_model] (P FIRST, along the sequence axis). INIT: paper compares random / sampled-vocab / class-label — class-label best (classification), sampled-vocab strong general default, random worst; HF default = RANDOM (used here — sampled-vocab needs an embedding table, not assumed by a standalone layer). k∈{1,5,20,100,150}, 20 a strong default. | R125 | xPos — length-extrapolatable positional encoding (Sun et al. 2022 arXiv:2212.10554 §3.2 Eq6/9/Alg1, "A Length-Extrapolatable Transformer"; microsoft/torchscale xpos_relative_position.py; used by RetNet §R114; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs paper Alg.1 + torchscale, NOT /deep-research). xPos = the UNCHANGED RoPE rotation (θ_i=base^(−2i/hd), base 10000) PLUS a per-pair magnitude scale ζ_i^(±n): query fq(q,n)=RoPE(q,n)·ζ^n (XPosDownscale false), key fk(k,m)=RoPE(k,m)·ζ^(−m) (true) → attention score picks up exponential ζ^(n−m) decay in relative distance (length extrapolation). ζ_i=(i/(hd/2)+γ)/(1+γ), i∈[0,hd/2), γ=0.4 (torchscale/RetNet default; paper says γ manually set). SAME ζ_i^n on BOTH elements of pair i. ξ=0 ⇒ pure RoPE. NUMERICAL VARIANTS OMITTED (torchscale-only, absent from paper): scale_base=512 exponent divisor + midpoint recentering min_pos=−(len+offset)//2 — paper uses raw position n (documented, like §R114's omitted GroupNorm). | R124 | DARE — Drop And REscale (Yu et al. 2024 arXiv:2311.03099 §3.1, ICML, "LMs are Super Mario"; mergekit; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs paper §3.1 + mergekit, NOT /deep-research). DROP: i.i.d. per-parameter Bernoulli — keep w.p. 1−p, drop (→0) w.p. p (paper m≈Bernoulli(p), δ̃=(1−m)⊙δ ≡ keep-mask Bernoulli(1−p)). RESCALE: survivors ÷(1−p), factor EXACTLY 1/(1−p) (δ̂=δ̃/(1−p); mergekit `res/=density`, density=1−p). UNBIASED: E[m]=1−p ⇒ E[δ̂]=δ ("approximate original embeddings" — the stated rationale). Result θ_pre+δ̂ per model, then combined by a downstream merge → DARE-linear (Task Arithmetic) or DARE-TIES (§R123). Drops p=0.9–0.99 of SFT deltas with negligible loss (they're redundant). | R123 | TIES-Merging — TrIm, Elect Sign & Merge (Yadav et al. 2023 arXiv:2306.01708 §3/Alg.1, NeurIPS; mergekit; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs paper §3 + mergekit, NOT /deep-research). Merges N models fine-tuned from a shared base θ_init into one, resolving interference. (1) TASK VECTORS τ_t=θ_t−θ_init per model. (2) TRIM per-parameter-tensor (NOT global): keep top density·numel entries by \|magnitude\|, rest→0 (paper k=20% ⇒ density 0.2). (3) ELECT SIGN per coordinate γ_p=sign(Σ_t τ̂_t^p) (greater total magnitude wins). (4) DISJOINT MERGE: τ_merged^p=(1/\|A_p\|)Σ_{t∈A_p} τ̂_t^p, A_p={t:sign(τ̂_t^p)=γ_p} — MEAN over the sign-AGREEING count (÷\|A_p\|, NOT ÷N; matches paper + mergekit normalize=True default); no agreeing entry ⇒ 0. (5) θ_merged=θ_init+λ·τ_merged, λ default 1 (tuned [0.8,1.8]). Beats plain task-vector averaging (which cancels opposing edits). Pure tensor math (no autograd op — one-shot post-training utility). matches nn.TIESMerge(base, models, density, lambda). §V16 tier-1: merge_test.go — SingleModel identity (density1/λ1 recovers the model) + SignElection (hand {+3,+1,−2}→mean{+3,+1}=2, discard −2) + Trim (top-density by \|mag\|) + Lambda (nonzero base + λ=0.5 hand) + ZeroSumStaysBase (perfect cancel → base) + errors | Yadav 2023 arXiv:2306.01708 + mergekit (PAPER = tier2 final §V16) | high |
| R122 | (IA)³ — Infused Adapter by Inhibiting and Amplifying Inner Activations (Liu et al. 2022 arXiv:2205.05638 §3.3; HF PEFT ia3; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs paper §3.3 + PEFT docs, NOT /deep-research). | R121 | CPO — Contrastive Preference Optimization (Xu et al. 2024 arXiv:2401.08417 eq3-5; TRL CPOTrainer; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs paper Eq.2/3/5 + TRL docs, NOT /deep-research). | R120 | Cholesky decomposition + SPD solve (numpy.linalg.cholesky / LAPACK dpotrf+dpotrs / gonum mat.Cholesky; Golub & Van Loan §4.2.1-4.2.5 Cholesky-Banachiewicz; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous zero-contradiction vs numpy/LAPACK + G&VL, NOT /deep-research). Definitional (numpy/textbook = §V16 tier-2). For real SYMMETRIC POSITIVE-DEFINITE (SPD) A: A=L·Lᵀ, L LOWER-triangular with L[i,i]>0 (numpy default UPLO='L'). CHOLESKY-BANACHIEWICZ recurrence: for j=0..n−1: L[j,j]=√(A[j,j]−Σ_{k<j}L[j,k]²); for i=j+1..n−1: L[i,j]=(A[i,j]−Σ_{k<j}L[i,k]·L[j,k])/L[j,j]. NO pivoting (SPD needs none; numerically stable). SPD TEST: factor succeeds ⟺ A SPD; the √ argument becomes ≤0 EXACTLY when A not positive-definite (LAPACK dpotrf returns INFO=j at the failing leading minor of order j) — the standard definitional SPD check. numpy.linalg.cholesky assumes A symmetric (reads one triangle, no symmetrize), raises LinAlgError on non-SPD. SPD SOLVE A·x=b (dpotrs): forward-sub L·y=b (y[i]=(b[i]−Σ_{k<i}L[i,k]y[k])/L[i,i]) then back-sub Lᵀ·x=y (x[i]=(y[i]−Σ_{k>i}L[k,i]x[k])/L[i,i]). ≈n³/3 flops = ≈2× faster than LU (2n³/3); standard direct solver for SPD systems (normal equations, covariance, Gaussian processes). matches linalg.Cholesky/CholSolve (validates square+symmetric rel-tol, input never mutated). §V16 tier-1: cholesky_test.go — Reconstruct (A=L·Lᵀ + L lower-tri + L[i,i]>0, n=1..8 on A=B·Bᵀ+nI) + CholSolve (A·x=b residual + ==LU Solve + multi-RHS [n,k]) + NonSPD ([[1,2],[2,1]] indefinite + negative diag rejected) + non-symmetric/non-square errors + ExampleCholesky | numpy.linalg.cholesky + LAPACK dpotrf/dpotrs + Golub & Van Loan §4.2 (REF = tier2 final §V16) | high |
| R118 | SVD-derived matrix quantities + matrix norms (numpy.linalg pinv/matrix_rank/cond/norm; Golub & Van Loan §2.3 norms + §5.5.2 pseudoinverse; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs numpy docs + G&VL, NOT /deep-research). Definitional (numpy/textbook = §V16 tier-2), all derived from the §R117-verified SVD. PINV (Moore-Penrose A⁺): A⁺=V·Σ⁺·Uᵀ, Σ⁺=diag(1/σᵢ if σᵢ>cutoff else 0), cutoff=rcond·σ_max, numpy default rcond=1e-15. Satisfies the 4 MP props (AA⁺A=A, A⁺AA⁺=A⁺, (AA⁺)ᵀ=AA⁺, (A⁺A)ᵀ=A⁺A); full-rank tall → A⁺=(AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ (=least-squares). RANK=count(σ>tol), tol=σ_max·max(m,n)·eps (numpy default, eps≈2.22e-16 f64). COND₂=σ_max/σ_min, +∞ if σ_min=0. NORMS: Frobenius=√Σaᵢⱼ²; induced-1=max_j Σ_i\|aᵢⱼ\| (max COL sum); induced-∞=max_i Σ_j\|aᵢⱼ\| (max ROW sum); induced-2=σ_max. matches linalg.Pinv/Rank/Cond/Norm2/NormFro/Norm1/NormInf. §V16 tier-1: derived_test.go — PinvMoorePenrose (4 props @1e-8 tall/square/wide + A⁺b==Lstsq) + PinvEqualsInverse + Rank (I/rank-1/zero/singular) + Cond (I=1, diag=2.5, singular=+Inf) + Norms (hand-computed Fro/1/∞/2) | numpy.linalg docs + Golub & Van Loan §2.3/§5.5.2 (REF = tier2 final §V16) | high |
| R117 | SVD via one-sided Jacobi (Hestenes) (Golub & Van Loan §8.6.3, Demmel "Applied Numerical Linear Algebra" §5.4.3, Hestenes J.SIAM 6:1958; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs G&VL/Demmel/Hestenes, NOT /deep-research). Definitional numerical algorithm (canonical textbook = §V16 tier-2). Reduced A=U·Σ·Vᵀ, p=min(m,n): U [m×p] orthonormal cols, Σ=diag(σ₁≥…≥σ_p≥0), V [n×p] orthonormal. METHOD: orthogonalize A's COLUMNS by right-applied Jacobi rotations A←A·J (accumulate V←V·J from I). Per pair i<j: α=‖aᵢ‖², β=‖aⱼ‖², γ=aᵢᵀaⱼ; if γ≈0 skip; else ζ=(β−α)/(2γ), t=sign(ζ)/(\|ζ\|+√(1+ζ²)) (smaller root \|θ\|≤π/4), c=1/√(1+t²) (NOT 1/(1+t²) — a common typo), s=c·t; aᵢ'=c·aᵢ−s·aⱼ, aⱼ'=s·aᵢ+c·aⱼ (exactly zeros aᵢ'ᵀaⱼ'). SWEEP cyclic-by-row until every \|γ\|/√(αβ)<tol (quadratic convergence). EXTRACT σⱼ=‖aⱼ‖ (final col norms), uⱼ=aⱼ/σⱼ, V=accumulated; sort σ DESCENDING, permute U/V cols; σⱼ=0→arbitrary uⱼ. m<n handled by SVD(Aᵀ) then swap U↔V. Backward-stable, HIGH RELATIVE ACCURACY for small σ (avoids κ²(A) of forming AᵀA). matches linalg.SVD. §V16 tier-1: svd_test.go — Reconstruct (U·Σ·Vᵀ==A + UᵀU=I + VᵀV=I + σ descending≥0, over m×n tall/square/wide 1..10) + Diagonal (σ=sorted \|diag\|) + rank-1 (σ=[5,0]) + errors | Golub & Van Loan §8.6.3 + Demmel §5.4.3 + Hestenes 1958 (REF = tier2 final §V16) | high |
| R116 | QR decomposition via Householder reflections + least-squares (Golub & Van Loan §5.1-5.2 Householder/QR + §5.3.3 least-squares; LAPACK dgeqrf/dorgqr/dgels; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs LAPACK dlarfg/dgeqrf/dgels + G&VL, NOT /deep-research). Definitional (canonical textbook/LAPACK = §V16 tier-2). For m×n A (m≥n): reduced A=Q·R, Q∈R^{m×n} orthonormal cols (QᵀQ=I), R∈R^{n×n} upper. HOUSEHOLDER reflector H=I−β·v·vᵀ maps x→α·e₁: α=−sign(x₀)·‖x‖₂ (sign OPPOSITE x₀ so v₀=x₀−α=x₀+sign(x₀)‖x‖ avoids cancellation), v=x−α·e₁, β=2/(vᵀv), R[k,k]=α. RIGHT-LOOKING: per col k build reflector from A[k:m,k], apply H_k to trailing A[k:m,k:n] (A_sub−β·v·(vᵀA_sub)), store v below diag. Q=H_0·…·H_{n−1} (reflectors applied in reverse onto I's first n cols). LEAST-SQUARES min‖Ax−b‖ (m≥n): c=Qᵀb (reflectors forward), back-solve R·x=c[0:n], residual=‖c[n:m]‖ — stabler than normal eqns AᵀAx=Aᵀb. Householder QR backward-stable (unlike classical Gram-Schmidt). matches linalg.QR + Lstsq. §V16 tier-1: qr_test.go — QRReconstruct (Q·R==A @1e-9 + QᵀQ==I + R upper, over m×n=1..10×1..8) + LstsqSquare (A·x==b) + LstsqOverdetermined (normal eq AᵀAx==Aᵀb @1e-8) + LineFit (exact y=2x+1) + errors | Golub & Van Loan §5.1-5.3 + LAPACK dgeqrf/dgels (REF-IMPL = tier2 final §V16) | high |
| R115 | LU decomposition with partial pivoting + derived determinant/solve/inverse (Golub & Van Loan "Matrix Computations" §3.2 LU/GEPP + §3.4 det; LAPACK dgetf2/dgetrs/dgetri; research-lite CONFIRMED 3-agent unanimous vs LAPACK reference + G&VL, NOT /deep-research). Definitional numerical algorithm (no paper; canonical textbook/LAPACK = §V16 tier-2). LU/GEPP right-looking Doolittle: factor P·A=L·U (L unit-lower, U upper); per column k pivot p=argmax_{i≥k}\|A[i,k]\| (max-abs, stability), swap rows k,p (record permutation + swap count), m=A[i,k]/A[k,k] stored in L[i,k], A[i,j]−=m·A[k,j] for i,j>k. DET=sign·Π_k U[k,k], sign=(−1)^(#swaps); singular (det=0) iff any U[k,k]=0. SOLVE A·x=b: permute Pb, forward-subst L·y=Pb (unit-L, y[i]=Pb[i]−Σ_{j<i}L[i,j]y[j]), back-subst U·x=y (x[i]=(y[i]−Σ_{j>i}U[i,j]x[j])/U[i,i]). INVERSE: one LU + solve A·X=I column-by-column (explicit inverse discouraged vs solving but correct when the inverse itself is needed). (A) SWA (Stochastic Weight Averaging, Izmailov/Podoprikhin/Garipov/Vetrov/Wilson 2018 arXiv:1803.05407): EQUAL-weight running average of parameter snapshots captured periodically (end of each cyclical/high-constant-LR cycle). (B) weight-EMA (Polyak & Juditsky 1992; ubiquitous in diffusion + LLM eval): EXPONENTIAL average w_EMA ← decay·w_EMA + (1−decay)·w every step, init to current weights, decay≈0.999–0.9999 (torch get_ema_avg_fn `decay*averaged+(1−decay)*param`, default 0.999). ## §V — verification invariants

V22 BOTTLENECK-MEASURED: a "the floor/bottleneck is X" attribution is a MEASURABLE claim, ⊥ an assumption — before recording it as fact OR building an optimization on it, A/B it by forcing the suspected cost OFF (e.g. force-disable the copy / the alloc / the dispatch) and comparing same-session medians. If removing X ⊥ moves the number, X is not the bottleneck. Prevents §B42-class waste (3 notes asserted a memcpy floor never measured; zero-copy built on it → 0 delta → reverted).

V23 CGO0-COMPILES-TESTS: the pure-Go gate runs `CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet ./...` (or `go test`), ⊥ `go build` alone — build skips _test.go files, so an untagged test file referencing cgo-only symbols passes build but breaks the suite (§B45). every cgo-backend test file carries its build tag; the gate must compile tests to enforce it

V24 SWEEP-BUDGET+EXIT: the full sweep runs `go test` with `-timeout 1800s` (llamagpu's trained-model suite legitimately exceeds the 600s default — §B46: 670s green vs FAIL at the default) AND checks the exit code UN-piped (`cmd > file; echo $?` — a trailing `| grep | tail` masks FAIL with exit 0, the §T447 lesson violated AGAIN in §T515). a sweep 'green' claim without both is void

V25 KERNELS-SEE-NO-RECORDER: backend.Execute strips the tape recorder from the ctx handed to kernels (recording happens ONCE, at the Execute choke point, after the kernel returns) — an in-kernel re-dispatch (ref fallback, ADR-0008 cpu routing) can therefore NEVER double-record an op and double its gradients (§B49 live occurrence, §T537's 46 latent sites, §T538 structural enforcement). the per-site .WithRecorder(nil) strips remain as documentation but are no longer load-bearing

V26 CI-SKIP FAILS OPEN: the docs-only change detector (internal/cichange) may skip CI ONLY on a POSITIVE proof that no code changed — every uncertain case (parse error, unknown file class, missing/unavailable base revision, workflow-file change, non-Go non-doc file, added/deleted files that are not pure docs) classifies as CODE and runs the full pipeline. asserted by unit tests per case. skipping is an optimization, never a correctness decision

V28 EXECUTE-SCREENS-ATTRS: backend.Execute rejects a NON-nil Attrs whose concrete type is not the one its op declares, BEFORE kernel resolution, naming op+got+want. this is what makes the codebase-wide `pa, _ := attrs.(backend.XAttrs)` idiom safe: discarding the `ok` is correct for nil (the convention for parameterless ops and ops relying on defaults) but a swallowed type MISMATCH hands the kernel a ZERO Attrs and returns a WRONG ANSWER with err==nil (§B69: OpSum+ConcatAttrs → scalar 28 instead of [6 22]). the op→type table is kept honest by a guard that NEVER READS IT — it derives ground truth from the kernels themselves (PC→function→ref-package AST→the assertions the kernel actually performs, following attrs into package-level helpers) and cross-examines Execute's public behaviour. a guard that read the table would only prove the table equals itself

V29 FOREIGN-PARSER-HOSTILE-GATED: every reader of a foreign format (npy, npz, safetensors, pytorch, gguf) rejects a malformed file with a CLEAN ERROR — never a panic, and never a wrong-but-nil-error tensor. concretely: shape products use the division-BEFORE-multiply guard (a post-multiply cap wraps and lets a hostile header through), negative dims are rejected, and no opcode/field parser indexes a stack or buffer without an emptiness check. each reader carries a hostile_test.go, and any fuzz target must actually REACH the parser under test — §B70's FuzzLoad fuzzed the zip container, so the pickle interpreter behind it was effectively unreachable (966k execs / 6 interesting) until a target taking raw inner bytes replaced it (5.77M / 104)

V30 SPECIAL-TOKENS-ARE-A-TRUST-BOUNDARY: a control/special token is minted ONLY from the specials-parsing path (EncodeSpecial), NEVER from untrusted text through plain Encode. this is a security property, not an ergonomic one: the chat template emits its markers as literal text, so if untrusted user content could encode to the same control ids it would forge conversation structure. two distinct paths must be closed and BOTH have been live (§B72) — the marker-matching pre-split (do it only on the trusted path) AND the segmentation algorithms themselves, since GGUF stores control tokens inside the main vocabulary and Unigram's Viterbi / WordPiece's MaxMatch search all of it. any new tokenizer or new segmentation path must gate on both; the injection case is a REQUIRED test, and it must be verified by mutation (rebuild the naive always-parse design and confirm the gate fails)

V31 ONE-DECODE-PATH-PER-ARCH: a model architecture's per-block features (biases, QK-norm, the Granite scalars) are applied in ONE place that every decode entry point routes through — DecodeStep, StreamStep and SelfExtendForward share a block stack whose only pluggable part is the attention core. duplicated decode logic drifts silently and asymmetrically (§B75: streaming dropped all six hooks while the normal path kept them, so the SAME model+prompt gave different tokens through different entry points, with no error). where a copy still exists it must be named in godoc and pinned by a cross-path equivalence test that (a) compares TOKENS not just logits, (b) uses NONZERO values for every feature per §B68, and (c) includes a feature-free control that passes in BOTH the broken and fixed states — without that control a failing gate cannot distinguish a real drift from a broken harness

V32 LOSSFREE-MOE-GATE: enabling auxiliary-loss-free MoE routing uses the paper's affinity exactly: s=sigmoid(routerLogit), TopK ranks s+b, and combine weights derive from s with b ABSENT (renormalization after selection allowed). the unoptioned Mixtral route remains softmax. required gates: a decisive case where sigmoid(logit)+b and logit+b select different experts, integrated Forward vs sigmoid reference, ForwardDecode equivalence, and router finite-difference gradcheck. bias is control state outside Params/autograd and updates only through the explicit per-batch sign rule (§B87/R242).

V33 EAGLE-LOSS-PAPER-EXACT: EagleLoss feature regression = mean SmoothL1_beta=1(pred,next), then +0.1*token CE; MSE proxy forbidden. Required decisive hand-reference includes abs(d)>1 linear branch, full head finite-diff grad, arbitrary-head lossless generation. (§B90/R256).

V34 QGALORE-PAPER-EXACT: default QGaLore = GaLore subspace + block-wise INT8 moments + packed affine INT4 projection + parameter-local adaptive SVD gap (official threshold/multiplier/window 0.4/2/5) + block-wise affine INT8 weights re-quantized by unbiased stochastic rounding. QuantBits 0 or 64 disables ALL four deltas and must remain bit-identical to GaLore across both projection sides and full rank. Required decisive gates: packed code/size/error bound, stable-subspace SVD-count reduction, both rounding branches + integrated weight-store mirror, convergence, deterministic seed. No end-to-end weight-memory claim while public Tensor keeps a float execution mirror (§B92/R259).

V35 APOLLO-SEED-ONLY-PROJECTION: APOLLO persistent matrix state = two-word projection seed + low-rank moments + limiter scalar; retaining the O(r·min(m,n)) Gaussian matrix is forbidden. P regenerates bit-identically from the seed on every use and changes only when Gap replaces that seed; reseeding preserves moment buffers. Required gates cover both projection sides, seed regeneration equality, Gap reseed difference, state shape, convergence and trajectory determinism (§B94/R258).

V36 SPEC-TABLE-INTEGRITY: SPEC.md §T/§B/§R/§V ids UNIQUE (monotonic, ⊥ reuse — B96) & ∀ §T row lives INSIDE the single contiguous §T GFM table (⊥ headerless fragment in another section — B97: EOF-appends after §B fed the 4-col §B table 6-col rows, 148 tasks GitHub-render-mangled, mdlint 166× table-ragged) & §T = LAST section of SPEC.md so append-at-EOF stays structurally correct & ∀ SPEC/worker-spec table mdlint-green. enforced: internal/mdlint repo test (already CI-side) + T886 spec-lint (id-uniqueness + §T-membership scan). [B96,B97]

V1 PARITY: ∀ op → golden test vs NumPy/torch within §R6 tol (f64 rtol 1e-12, f32 rtol 1e-5). missing golden → generate reproducibly + commit.

V2 GRAD: ∀ differentiable op → numeric gradient check (central finite diff) under rel 1e-4.

V3 CROSS: accel backend result == Pure-Go reference within backend tol defined by V11 (exact bit-match ⊥ required — SIMD/parallel reorders sums).

V4 PLATFORM: CI green ∀ {macOS, Windows, Linux} × {Pure-Go fallback + available accel}. missing accel → skip w/ log, ⊥ silent pass.

V5 BENCH: ∀ optimized op → benchmark + baseline number recorded. regression breaks CI.

V6 PROP: property-based tests (shape algebra, linearity, associativity where math-guaranteed).

V7 CGO: ⊥ cgo in ship path without green optimized Pure-Go ref + committed benchmark over §C.thr. `CGO_ENABLED=0` green everywhere.

V8 STABLE: public API changes only via documented deprecation path.

V9 TRUTH: Pure-Go reference backend = source of numeric truth; accel validated against it (⊥ vice versa).

V10 ACCUM: reduction & GEMM accumulation → f32 inputs accumulate in f64 (| Kahan) unless §R justifies else. parallel/goroutine reduction order documented; non-determinism only w/ §R-justified tol. guards non-associative FP [B6].

V11 CROSSTOL: ∀ accel op → backend tol documented per op, rtol scales w/ reduction length K (⊥ single fixed rtol). defines V3. established: elementwise (T11) & blocked-GEMM (T12/T12b) = exact (tol 0, same accum order); metal f32 GEMM (T20) = rtol(K)=1e-6·√K (MPS f32 accum + reorder) [B5].

V15 UNTRUSTED-IO: ∀ format reader (gguf/safetensors/npy) on hostile input → return error, NEVER panic/OOM/overflow. all length/dim/nesting claims capped BEFORE alloc (header ≤ cap, numel ≤ cap, array-depth ≤ 64, grow ⊥ pre-alloc-from-claim). GUARDED BY native fuzz tests (FuzzLoad/FuzzRead/FuzzRoundTrip) + hostile-input regressions [B28,B31,B32].

V16 VALIDATION-LADDER: ∀ ALGORITHM impl → 2 tiers, both required. tier1 = bit/tol parity vs a reference LIB (torch/sklearn/ggml-py/…). tier2 (FINAL authority) = the defining SCIENTIFIC paper/source (arXiv/DOI/canonical textbook) — implemented formula matches the paper's equation, cited in §R. tier1 alone ⊥ sufficient. FILE FORMATS have no paper → their reference SPEC/impl IS the definitional source (stated, ⊥ invent a paper). paper-tier status tracked per algorithm in §R.

V12 EDGE: ∀ op → documented policy for NaN/Inf (IEEE-754 propagate), empty tensor, zero-dim, non-contiguous view. golden ! include edge cases [B9].

V13 GOLDEN-REPRO: ∀ golden file → record generating env (lib+version, dtype, seed, shape) in sidecar. regeneration deterministic. guards V1 reproducibility [B8].

V14 BACKEND-EXEC: `Backend`/`Kernel` interface ! define execution/sync model (sync default; async accel exposes explicit `Synchronize()`) at T5, before any accel/T20. adding GPU ⊥ break V8 [B7].

V19 DOCS-GATE: internal/apicheck walks every public pkg via go/ast (parses SOURCE, ⊥ imports the pkgs → build-tagged cgo backends checked too) and FAILS on: (a) any exported symbol (func/type/method/const/var) lacking a godoc comment, incl. any exported STRUCT FIELD lacking a doc/inline comment (fields = public-facing API, "docs for everything public facing"); (b) any user-facing pkg with no `Example`; (c) any exported user-facing TYPE not shown in a runnable Example — coverage credited if the Type name, its `New<Type>` ctor, OR an `ExampleType`/`ExampleType_*` appears in any Example (bodies inspected via ast). section comments before a grouped const/var attach as doc to the first spec only → each grouped one-liner needs its own comment. (d) any exported METHOD on a user-facing type not exercised in any runnable Example — credited if the method name is CALLED in any Example body (ast-inspected selector calls) or an ExampleType_Method exists. per-type AND per-method rules each have a JUSTIFIED allowlist (typeExampleExempt / methodExampleExempt: interfaces, functional-option/callback func types, enums, config structs, fixture-heavy models, trivial accessors covered by the type example = "where meaningful"). runs as a normal test (`go test ./...`) + `make apicheck`; in `all`/`ci`. = mechanical enforcement of C10/V17/C13 BEFORE commit/push. exempts internal/* + backend impl subpkgs (blank-import registration, not public surface). guards C13.

V21 NO-MAGIC-STRINGS: internal/apicheck TestNoMagicBackendNameStrings walks every .go via go/ast (string BasicLits only → comments/import-paths ignored) & FAILS on any backend-name literal ("cpu"/"ref"/"metal"/"cuda"/"vulkan") outside the allowlist {backend/names.go = the Name enum def, tensor/device.go = the DeviceKind Stringer}. enforces §C15/ADR-0015: backends referenced by typed backend.Name constants, ⊥ bare literals. in `all`/`ci`.

V20 OP-PARAMS-TYPED: `backend.Attrs` is a sealed interface (`interface{ opAttrs() }`), never `map[string]any`; every op's params = a concrete struct impl (§I6/§C14/ADR-0014). guard test internal/apicheck TestNoStringKeyedAttrs greps the tree → FAILS if the accessor pattern (`attrs.Int(`/`.Bool(`/`.Float(`/`.Ints(` on an Attrs) or an `Attrs map[string]` decl reappears. defaults single-sourced in each struct's `WithDefaults` (kernel+VJP call it → ⊥ drift). construction wrong-field/type = compile error. in `all`/`ci`.

V18 AUTOSELECT: backend.Default() = highest-preference REGISTERED backend along the descending-performance order (default cuda>metal>vulkan>cpu, §R46), else the reference — the guaranteed final fallback, ALWAYS present. accel backends Register in init() ONLY when their device is detected (§V4 — ⊥ silent claim of an absent device). selection by preference order, ⊥ by registration/import order. order overridable via SetPreference; unknown names skipped safely. NewContext & autograd.NewTape use Default → building with an accel tag routes work to GPU w/ NO code change. GPU-first default justified by benchmark, ⊥ aspiration (§R46).

V17 DOCS: ∀ exported package & top-level symbol → godoc present, dual-audience (professional: math + §R paper-cite; layperson: plain what/why/when). ∀ user-facing package → runnable `Example` fns at ≥3 levels: trivial, realistic use-case, embedded-in-bigger-pipeline. examples live in `example_test.go`, verified by `// Output:` under `go test` (∴ docs ⊥ rot — CI runs them). new public API ⊥ "done" until its godoc + examples exist (part of task DoD). guards C10.

The other ≈63% is occupancy-bound (§B43: register-caching reads gave nothing). Atomic-free is STRUCTURALLY HARD: softmax is per-QUERY, so the natural per-query parallelization must scatter to keys (→ atomics); a per-key kernel would recompute softmax O(seq) times per key = O(seq³), worse. The only real fix = a TILED flash-backward (key tiles staged in threadgroup memory, dK/dV block-reduced across the threadgroup's queries, ONE atomic-flush per tile → ≈TG× fewer global atomics) — a big kernel project, and per §T349/§B43 M-series/MoltenVK opts are occupancy-limited so payoff is uncertain (est ≤1.2× on training). PARKED until a dedicated fire measures the tiled design in isolation. P1=r,Pᵀ1=c; solved via Gibbs kernel K=exp(−C/ε), iterate u←r⊘(Kv), v←c⊘(Kᵀu), plan P=diag(u)K diag(v). P≥0, row/col sums→r/c; const-shift-of-C invariance ⇒ min-cost numerical stabilization. | T317 | x | L3 Grokfast-MA gradient filter (Lee, Ahn, Kim & Kim 2024, §R153) — nn.GrokfastMA. The windowed moving-average variant of Grokfast-EMA (§T?/§R153): same idea (isolate + amplify the slow low-frequency gradient component that drives grokking → up to ≈50× faster generalization) but the low-pass filter is a plain MA over the last W raw gradients instead of an EMA. μ_t=mean(last W g) (or sum with FilterSum); ĝ_t=g_t+λ·μ_t passed to the base optimizer (drop-in pre-step transform, base unchanged). WARMUP (default true, matches ref): amplify ONLY once the window is full (first W−1 steps pass raw g through) — ref condition `not warmup or len==window_size and not trigger`. λ=0 = exact base no-op. Defaults λ=5.0, W=100, warmup=true, mean. NewGrokfastMA(base,params,opts…) + WithGrokfastMA{Lambda,Window,Warmup,Sum}; O(numel)/step via a per-param ring buffer + running sum (evict oldest when full). float64 state (§V10). §V16 tier-2: the Grokfast-MA variant was ALREADY CONFIRMED in the §R153 verdict ("Grokfast-MA variant (windowed deque, default window=100, λ=5.0) = follow-up"; vs ironjr/grokfast gradfilter_ma ref impl) — NO fresh research (research-lite weekly-limited until 2026-07-13; §V16 satisfied by existing §R153 tier-2). §V16 tier-1/§V2: grokfast_ma_test.go — MARecurrenceNoWarmup(deque mean across W-eviction == independent recompute @1e-12) + MAWarmupGating(first W−1 raw, then full-window mean amplified — the ref gate) + MASum(FilterSum uses window sum) + MALambdaZeroNoOp + MAConvergesSGD(§V2 convex quadratic) + ExampleGrokfastMA. | T318 | x | L1-ops sample variance/std with delta-degrees-of-freedom (numpy ddof, §R140 follow-up) — ops.VarDDof(x,axes,keepdims,ddof) + ops.StdDDof(…). Completes the §R140 var/std surface: existing Var/Std are population (ddof=0, ÷N); ddof divides the sum of squared deviations by (N−ddof), so ddof=1 = the UNBIASED sample variance (Bessel's correction), the standard estimator. Impl reuses the verified population Var and rescales by the EXACT factor N/(N−ddof) (since Var=SS/N ⇒ Var·N/(N−ddof)=SS/(N−ddof)); N=x.Numel()/v.Numel() (elements reduced per output entry, robust to nil/single/multi axes + keepdims). tensor.Full matches v's shape so no broadcast. Errors on ddof<0 or ddof≥N. | T319 | x | L3 CLIP contrastive loss with a LEARNED logit scale (Radford et al. 2021, §R165) — nn.CLIPLogitScale + nn.CLIPLoss(ctx,image,text,scale). Completes the CLIP form named in §R165 ("CLIP learns logit_scale=1/τ", open_clip loss.py): unlike InfoNCE's fixed temperature, CLIP trains a scalar and applies exp() of it as the logit multiplier so softmax sharpness is learned jointly with the encoders. CLIPLogitScale stores a rank-0 LOG-space param (LogScale; applied scale=exp(LogScale)), Params()={LogScale}, Scale()=exp float, and Clamp() caps it to [0,log(MaxScale)] between steps (open_clip logit_scale.clamp_(0,log(100)) — mutating, no grad). Defaults exp init 1/0.07 (CLIPInitScale), ceiling 100 (CLIPMaxScale). CLIPLoss = symmetric in-batch softmax-CE over S=exp(LogScale)·(î·t̂ᵀ) (î,t̂ = L2-normalized rows) = ½(CE(S,arange)+CE(Sᵀ,arange)); differentiable w.r.t. image, text AND the scale param (verified the broadcast-Mul VJP reduces the [n,n] grad to the rank-0 scalar). §V16 tier-2: the learned-logit-scale CLIP form was ALREADY CONFIRMED in the §R165 verdict (vs CLIP Fig.3 + open_clip loss.py: logit_scale learned, exp-applied, clamped) — NO fresh research (research-lite weekly-limited until 2026-07-13; §V16 satisfied by existing §R165 tier-2). §V16 tier-1/§V2: clip_test.go — CLIPLossEqualsInfoNCE(frozen scale ⇒ == verified InfoNCE(τ=1/exp(LogScale)) @1e-9 over scale∈{1,5,1/0.07} — anchors CLIP to the already-verified loss) + CLIPLossGradcheck(image,text,AND LogScale rank-0 == finite-diff) + CLIPClamp([1,MaxScale] ceiling+floor, in-range untouched) + CLIPInitAndParams(default 1/0.07, single param, init>max error) + CLIPLossErrors(shape mismatch, nil scale) + ExampleCLIPLogitScale. | T322 | x | L2 einsum reduction gradient — complete the OpEinsum VJP for single-operand reductions (§R142 follow-up) — autograd/vjp_einsum.go. | T323 | x | L2 einsum diagonal/trace gradient — complete the OpEinsum VJP for single-operand repeated indices (§R143; the last case R143 named UNSUPPORTED) — autograd/vjp_einsum.go. A REPEATED letter in operand k's subscript ("ii->i" diagonal, "ii->" trace, "iij->j") reads A_k on its GENERALIZED DIAGONAL (only entries where the repeated positions are equal contribute), so the gradient is nonzero ONLY on that diagonal. Fix: (1) collapse sₖ to its distinct letters dedupK (dedupSub, first-occurrence order); (2) compute the standard swap-rule gradient over dedupK (reusing §T322's reduction ones-injection, keyed on each letter's first position); (3) SCATTER it back onto A_k's shape via scatterDiag — dAₖ[idx]=gDedup[collapsed(idx)] iff idx is on the diagonal (all positions sharing a letter hold the same coordinate), else 0. Scoped to SINGLE operand: a repeat shared across MULTIPLE operands, and a repeated OUTPUT index (diagonalizes the output), still error (documented; forward works). Einsum is now fully differentiable except those two. §V16-exempt: DEFINITIONAL (§R143 = calculus of numpy.einsum backward; swap rule + diagonal scatter), no paper; numerically verified. §V2: einsum_test.go — EinsumGradcheck EXTENDED with diagonals (ii->i, ii->, iij->j == central finite-diff @1e-4, incl. off-diagonal zeros) + EinsumDiagonalGradScatter (closed form: "ii->i" ⇒ dA[i,j]=g_i·δ_ij, exact) + EinsumUnsupportedGradient reworked to the still-erroring cases (ii,ij->j multi-operand repeat + i->ii repeated-output; forward works, backward errors) + reduction/matmul closed-forms intact.
